one_liner: Paid civic letters with verified citations and delivery gates; watchlist until conversion is proven.

authority.decisionRecord: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption — operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record.

pomReviews.summary: Refresh completed with assumptions labeled; operator and market validation still required.

research.summary: Workspace-only review found a CivicState civic-letter product with real monorepo implementation evidence, stale planning contradictions, no live revenue evidence, and registry watchlist constraints.
methods: Read repo-local planning and master plan documents.
Inspected source structure to separate implemented code from aspirational roadmap.
Used bottom-up market sizing because network research was unavailable.
Tagged external market and competitor statements as assumptions.

planningMethod.evidenceHarvest: Preserve the CivicState product thesis, pricing, code evidence, registry watchlist note, and stale planning contradictions before adding market or financial claims.
planningMethod.marketResearch: Workspace-only mode prevented refreshed external market research, so market sizing is bottom-up and labeled as assumption.
planningMethod.financialValidation: Revenue is modeled as paid campaigns multiplied by average order value, with costs derived from repo pricing and master-plan unit economics.
planningMethod.alternativeSearch: Compared transactional citizen letters, organizational advocacy SaaS, free civic messaging, and generic AI drafting as strategic alternatives.
planningMethod.antiPlan: Attacked the plan for weak willingness to pay, deliverability risk, legal/citation risk, official data quality, and generic AI substitution.
planningMethod.finalSynthesis: Hold at needs-revision until operator resolves identity/posture and real validation proves paid conversion, coverage, deliverability, and safety.

segments.name: U.S. residents with concrete civic issues
segments.painfulJob: They need to turn a civic concern into a credible, correctly routed, citation-backed constituent letter without doing manual legal and official research.

currentSubstitutes: Manual official lookup and self-written email.
Free civic messaging tools such as Resistbot.
Generic AI assistants used for drafting only.
Enterprise advocacy platforms that serve organizations rather than individuals.
willingnessToPayEvidence: Repo pricing route and master plan encode $5, $15, and $25 transactional tiers.
No workspace evidence of paid conversion or live revenue was found.
Willingness to pay remains an assumption until a paid preview funnel runs.

market.category: Consumer civic-action workflow and citation-backed constituent communication.
market.competitiveLandscape: Substitutes include free civic messaging, petitions, manual emails, generic AI drafting, and enterprise advocacy tools; CivicState must win by completing research, routing, compliance, and delivery.
market.wedge: Start with paid, human-reviewed, email-delivered issue categories where correct official routing and cited research are visibly valuable.

businessModel.valueCreation: Convert user issue text and ZIP code into researched, moderated, citation-backed letters to matched officials.
businessModel.valueDelivery: Web submission funnel, AI research/drafting workers, official lookup, Stripe payment, Postmark delivery, dashboard, and admin review.
businessModel.valueCapture: One-time paid delivery packages at $5, $15, and $25, with future expansion blocked until the core loop proves itself.
businessModel.pricing: $5 single, $15 three-pack, and $25 full-spread tiers from repo plan and payment route.
businessModel.revenuePath: Preview before payment, payment before delivery, then opt-in public campaign pages and partnerships only after validation.
businessModel.unitEconomics: Base model uses $18 average order value and approximately 90.1% gross margin, both assumption-tagged in BUSINESS.md.
businessModel.operatingCosts: AI model calls, email delivery, Stripe fees, hosting, monitoring, official data providers, human review, compliance, and support.
businessModel.marginLogic: Margins remain attractive only if citation verification, moderation, and official lookup can run with low human-review load.

financialModel.summary: Validation model: 2,400 paid campaigns at $18 AOV produce $43,200 revenue in the first proof year, with assumptions labeled in BUSINESS.md.
financialModel.validationStatus: Needs operator and market validation; not approved as forecast.
revenueAssumptions: Average order value is $18 from a blended $5/$15/$25 tier mix.
First proof year can reach 2,400 paid campaigns through narrow issue wedges.
costAssumptions: Variable cost begins near $1.78 per paid campaign.
Fixed costs through the first proof year stay near $18,000.
Operator review burden stays below 30 minutes per day.
sensitivityTests: At 1.0% paid conversion, first proof-year revenue falls to $14,400.
Government inbox placement below 85% blocks launch even if conversion works.
Variable cost doubling to $3.56 per campaign preserves gross margin but may expose support burden.

alternatives.name: Transactional citizen letter product
alternatives.thesis: Individuals will pay a small amount when the product completes research, routing, drafting, and delivery.
alternatives.expectedUpside: A narrow paid workflow can validate quickly and generate reusable issue/citation data.
alternatives.financialCase: Low average order value but high gross margin if automation works.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Selected as the current plan because it matches repo implementation and pricing.

alternatives.name: Organizational advocacy SaaS
alternatives.thesis: Nonprofits, HOAs, or local groups may pay more for campaign tooling.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Higher contract values and repeat usage.
alternatives.financialCase: Could support subscription revenue, but sales cycles and product requirements expand materially.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Deferred because the repo and master plan explicitly prioritize the individual citizen pipeline first.

alternatives.name: Research-only civic assistant
alternatives.thesis: Users may want citation-backed research without platform delivery.
alternatives.financialCase: Likely lower willingness to pay and weaker differentiation versus generic AI.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Rejected for now because delivery completion is the main differentiated job.

antiPlan.summary: The plan fails if users will not pay, officials do not receive emails, citation/legal risk is unacceptable, or generic AI satisfies the need.

holes.whyItMatters: Without paid conversion, the repo is a civic research tool rather than a business.
holes.repair: Run a capped paid preview funnel and require measured conversion before scale.

holes.whyItMatters: If letters land in spam or bounce, the product breaks its core promise.
holes.repair: Complete deliverability warm-up and per-domain reporting before public launch.

holes.hole: Citation and legal-risk posture may be too fragile.
holes.whyItMatters: A fabricated citation, threatening content, or legal-advice confusion can create trust and compliance failure.
holes.repair: Keep citation verification, moderation, disclaimers, human review, and audit logs as launch gates.

holes.hole: Local official data may be incomplete or expensive.
holes.whyItMatters: Poor local coverage reduces value for many civic issues.
holes.repair: Run provider coverage/cost tests before broad geographic launch.

mitigations: Keep launch scope narrow and manually reviewed.
Measure conversion, coverage, deliverability, citation QA, refunds, and operator time before scale.
Resolve platform posture before duplicating long-term auth, billing, and identity work.
Treat all external market claims as assumptions until refreshed research is allowed.
residualRisks: Free substitutes may cap average order value.
Provider policy, government spam filters, or official opt-outs may reduce delivery reliability.
Legal/compliance review may require product changes that lower conversion.
The operator may decide this remains a personal/research asset, not a business.

strategy.diagnosis: CivicState has a coherent product and some implementation, but no workspace proof of market pull or launch safety.
strategy.guidingPolicy: Validate the smallest paid, compliant, delivered civic-letter loop before expanding features or investment posture.
strategy.whereToPlay: U.S. residents with concrete civic issues where cited research and correct routing matter.
strategy.howToWin: Complete the full job with verified citations, official matching, moderation, payment-before-delivery, and delivery tracking.
strategy.moatHypothesis: Verified citation history, official contact freshness, delivery/bounce data, moderation/audit logs, and issue templates can compound if usage exists.
coherentActions: Resolve project identity mismatch before publication.
Run official coverage and deliverability audits.
Instrument funnel economics by pricing tier.
Keep human review gates until safety data exists.
tradeoffs: Do not build organizational SaaS before proving individual paid demand.
Do not treat the repo as investible until operator promotes it from watchlist.
Do not scale automated sending before deliverability and moderation proof.

channels: Issue-intent SEO after opt-in public campaign pages exist.
Local civic, tenant, parent, and neighborhood group partnerships.
Constrained metro or issue-category launch with manual QA.
Product-led preview funnel with payment before delivery.
assumptions: Users will value completion of research, routing, and delivery more than free drafting alone.
Narrow issue wedges will convert better than broad civic-tech messaging.
Partnerships can provide early trust while SEO takes time.

jobs: Review flagged submissions and defamation/safety risks.
Inspect citation verification failures and human-review queues.
Monitor delivery, bounces, spam complaints, refunds, and treasury status.
Maintain official contact data and opt-out suppressions.
aiNativeAutomationTargets: Classify civic issue, jurisdiction, severity, and categories.
Research public legal sources and verify citations.
Draft personalized letters with disclosures and disclaimers.
Send letters only after payment and delivery gates clear.
Summarize metrics for operator launch decisions.

regulatory: No legal advice or regulatory filing posture.
CAN-SPAM, AI disclosure, privacy, and opt-out obligations must remain explicit.
External legal conclusions require operator/legal review.
privacy: Civic concern text, identity, ZIP, and political opinions are sensitive.
Tier One fields require encryption and deletion workflows as planned.
security: Clerk auth, Stripe webhooks, Postmark webhooks, and admin routes must remain protected.
Append-only audit and ledger records must retain HMAC checks.
Secrets and provider keys must not move into docs.
brand: Non-partisan constituent communication, not lobbying firm branding.
No claim of guaranteed official action.
operational: Workspace-only review means no external claims are evidence.
Registry watchlist posture blocks investible claims.
Operator must decide whether WrkPlug shared rails apply.

successMetrics: Government-domain inbox placement at or above 85%.
Federal/state official coverage at or above 95%.
Operator routine load below 30 minutes per day.
killTriggers: Paid conversion below 1.0% after a fair launch test.
Citation QA produces unresolved fabricated or unsafe outputs.
Operator chooses to keep the project as research only.
pivotTriggers: Organizations show stronger willingness to pay than individuals.
Local official coverage is too weak for individual use cases.
reviseTriggers: WrkPlug shared rails become available and reduce standalone infra rationale.
Provider costs materially exceed the unit model.
Legal review changes permissible product claims.
wakeConditions: Operator confirms CivicState should pitch as a business.
Paid conversion, deliverability, and coverage gates are documented.
A narrow launch wedge shows repeatable acquisition.

aiWorkGovernance.wedge: AI assists civic research and drafting, but human and system gates control moderation, citations, payment, and delivery.
aiWorkGovernance.problem: Raw AI drafting can hallucinate citations, misroute messages, or amplify unsafe user content.
aiWorkGovernance.promise: CivicState should constrain AI to verified sources, logged actions, explicit disclosures, and operator review for risky cases.
duplicatePrevention: Official lookup and cached contacts prevent repeated manual research.
Citation verification strips unverified references before delivery.
Roadmap checkboxes tie work to business-plan headings before implementation.
coordinationMetrics: Submissions flagged or blocked by moderation.
Letters sent, delivered, bounced, failed, or suppressed.
Operator review queue depth and age.
tokenSpendControls: Token usage logged per agent action.
Budget and treasury monitoring before scale.
aiWorkGovernance.risk: AI output can create legal, safety, or trust exposure if verification and moderation gates are bypassed.

items: Whether the dispatch project identity should remain brooks-history or be corrected to CivicState.
Whether users pay for the full job rather than use free AI drafting.
Whether government inbox placement is good enough for launch.
Whether local official data coverage is strong enough.
Whether operator/legal review accepts the compliance posture.
Whether WrkPlug shared rails should replace standalone auth and billing.

experiments.question: Will users pay after preview?
experiments.method: Run a capped paid funnel with tier-specific tracking.

experiments.question: Can the product reliably reach officials?
experiments.method: Run monitored domain warming and government-domain delivery tests.
experiments.successSignal: Inbox placement at or above 85% with acceptable bounce and complaint rates.

experiments.question: Does official lookup cover target use cases?
experiments.method: Audit selected ZIP codes against manual lookup and provider results.
experiments.successSignal: Federal/state coverage at or above 95% and local coverage sufficient for selected wedges.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Users will pay an $18 blended average order value.
assumptionLedger.evidence: Repo has $5, $15, and $25 tiers; no live revenue evidence.
assumptionLedger.challenge: Free AI drafting may satisfy the job.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Deliverability can exceed 85% for government domains.
assumptionLedger.evidence: Planning names deliverability as a validation gate; code includes Postmark delivery and bounce handling.
assumptionLedger.challenge: Government spam filtering may be stricter than normal transactional email.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Official coverage can exceed 95% for federal/state.
assumptionLedger.evidence: Planning names congress.gov and OpenStates, and code includes lookup adapters.
assumptionLedger.challenge: ZIP-to-district mapping and local coverage may be incomplete.

assumptionLedger.evidence: Business model arithmetic uses repo pricing and master-plan costs.
assumptionLedger.challenge: Human review, refunds, provider costs, or model costs may rise.

assumptionLedger.assumption: WrkPlug shared rails will be available and desirable.
assumptionLedger.evidence: EIR brief requires Platform Posture section; repo currently uses standalone Clerk, Stripe, and Postmark.
assumptionLedger.challenge: WrkPlug Phase Zero is not signed and operator may leave CivicState standalone.
